name: agent-bridge-concurrent-flip
description: Tier-P F1 version-flip coherence scenario: install + provision agent-bridge on a fresh box, then drive the REAL immutable-runtime layout manager (versioned_runtime -- atomic current-version publish via os.replace + a current -> last-known-good -> newest resolver) under a STORM of racing installers and assert the invariant that makes a concurrent plugin update safe -- while multiple installers race to flip the active version (the effect of several new Copilot sessions each firing the sessionStart-hook reinstall at once), a reader resolving the runtime must ALWAYS land on a valid, existing version slot, never a torn/half-written current-version marker or a pointer to a slot that isn't there. Third leg of the concurrent-update triad: agent-bridge-concurrent-relay (the relay recovers), agent-bridge-concurrent-daemon (a duplicate daemon is refused), and this (the version flip stays coherent). Checks: (flip-storm-coherent-resolution) two installers race to flip current-version between two valid slots; over thousands of reads the resolver always returns an existing slot python (never None, never a missing path) and both versions are observed active; (marker-never-torn) the raw current-version marker is never empty/partial during the storm (os.replace atomicity). FIDELITY: a fully live 'two real installers race the sessionStart hook + a live daemon end-to-end' assertion is a Tier-E concern; this Tier-P probe proves the version-resolution MECHANISM. The probe is portable stdlib-only (drives the real versioned_runtime with cross-process flippers), so it is verifiable off-Docker too. Name-free / public.

stages.title: version-slot flip coherence under racing installers
